text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"The bounded‑memory variant remains accurate because limiting the stored item count prevents cross‑fact interference; this mechanism mirrors the effect of periodic consolidation that compresses context, implying that adding a consolidation step to an unbounded append system should recover flat recall without explicitly truncating memory","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["93ae3681","e8af7ee8","45562236","800e430c"],"tags":["consolidation","interference","memory‑management","accuracy"]},{"statement":"A sliding‑window memory of size ≈40 items will match the bounded‑memory variant’s stable recall, suggesting that the effective capacity limit causing the accuracy drop can be addressed either by a hard window or by rewrite‑based consolidation; this can be validated by the rewrite‑vs‑append ablation sweeps","confidence":0.71,"support_ids":["e8af7ee8","d421fc37","93ae3681","853b30eb"],"tags":["ablation","windowed‑memory","interference","recall"]}]}
